A definitive agreement was signed on 29 April 2026 to sell the Long Ridge power plant to MARA for about $1.52 billion, the regulatory application was filed on 8 May in docket EC26-92, the buyer cleared its bondholder consents in June, no financing contingency exists, and management has guided to approval by the middle of the third quarter. There is no wash-out worth waiting for; this is the wash-out. Two things keep this from being the maximum-conviction version of this setup. The first is the floor. What the market is pricing is the 30 March 2026 data on elegrobart, the under-the-skin follow-on. DDL.dated_milestone:

Shareholder approval completed 27 March 2026 at the annual general meeting in Shanghai, where every resolution passed including the authority to return not less than 90% of post-closing cash. Contractual outside date: the agreement may be terminated if closing has not occurred within twelve months of signing, which is about 5 February 2027, extendable by mutual consent.

Verified as of 28 July 2026: the transaction has NOT closed and no clearance has been announced. The issuer's most recent statement on it, in the first-quarter release of 21 May 2026, says the deal "has not been completed, and is subject to ... receipt of anti-monopoly clearance from the SAMR." No company announcement on the transaction has followed. Chinese commentary as of 12 June 2026 noted the regulator had not publicly disclosed any progress. One conflicting secondary Chinese source paraphrases Meituan as saying the merger-control filing cleared; it is contradicted by the issuer's own dated disclosure and by the absence of any closing, so it is not treated as established.

Caveat on dating: the only hard calendar date in the file is the 5 February 2027 outside date, and it is extendable. The event that actually gates closing - the competition regulator's decision - carries no published decision date and none is obtainable, which is a feature of the Chinese merger-review regime rather than evidence of drift. Chinese business coverage also reports a 31 August 2026 deadline for the pre-closing cash withdrawal from the China subsidiary; that date could not be re-verified from a primary document and is carried as unverified. It is not part of this valuation, but if real it is a free read on the process in about five weeks.

The core judgement is straightforward. Scholar Rock has a hard, dated, binding regulatory decision 65 days away, and the reason the last one went wrong has been engineered around rather than merely promised away. The FDA's September 2025 refusal came out of a routine general site inspection of Catalent Indiana, the contract manufacturer that fills the vials - observations the company states were 'not specific to apitegromab', in a letter that 'did not cite any other approvability concerns'. Nothing was wrong with the medicine, and the Phase 3 data that made this company remains untouched. Scholar Rock then did the right thing: rather than wait for Catalent to be cured, it resubmitted on 31 March 2026 with a second U.S. fill-finish site written into the application, and the FDA accepted with a 30 September 2026 action date and no advisory committee.

The timing call rests on a specific market error. Over the past week investors sold an American catalyst on European news.
